title: Validate a thermostat target before anything changes

blocks.text: *Fail fast*: validate the arguments at the start of a method and throw at once, before any state has changed. Write `Thermostat`:

items: `Thermostat()` starts with target `20` and an empty history.
`void setTarget(Integer celsius)` accepts a target from `5` to `30` inclusive: it becomes the target and is appended to the history.
a `null` target throws `NullPointerException` with the message `celsius` (`Objects.requireNonNull` does this in one call);
a target out of range throws `IllegalArgumentException("Target out of range: <celsius>")`.
`int getTarget()` and `List<Integer> history()` (the accepted targets, oldest first). Whether the returned list is a copy or a view is up to you; the tests only read it.

blocks.text: Once a `throw` runs, nothing after it in the method runs, so where you put the checks decides what a failed call leaves behind.

cases.says: A target in range becomes the target and joins the history; one out of range throws IllegalArgumentException.
The message says what was wrong and with which value: "Target out of range: 42".
The check runs before any state changes, so a rejected target leaves the target and the history as they were.
A null target fails fast with a NullPointerException whose message is "celsius".

concepts: Arguments are validated at the start of a method, before any state changes.
Objects.requireNonNull documents a null check and fails fast with a named message.
A throw ends the method at once, so no statement after it runs.
